questions.text:
मोहित ने दो क्षेत्रो 'A' तथा 'B' से एकत्रित मृदा (मिट्टी) के दो नमूनों का विश्लेषण किया। उसने इन परिणामों को रिकॉर्ड किया :
मृदा नमूना A : लिग्निन 40%, शर्करा 10%, काइटिन 45%, नाइट्रोजन 5%
मृदा नमूना B : लिग्निन 5%, शर्करा 35%, काइटिन 15%, नाइट्रोजन 45%
उपरोक्त दोनों नमूनों से मिट्टी में विघटन की दर को निम्नलिखित में से किस विकल्प में सही प्रकार से दर्शाया गया है ?
questions.text_english:
Mohit performed an analysis of two different soil samples from two areas A and B. He recorded these results:
Soil Sample A: Lignin 40%, Sugar 10%, Chitin 45%, Nitrogen 5%
Soil Sample B: Lignin 5%, Sugar 35%, Chitin 15%, Nitrogen 45%
Which of these is true about their rate of decomposition in both the soil?
questions.instruction_line: सर्वोचित विकल्प का चयन कर उत्तर लिखिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select and write the correct choice.

options.A: मिट्टी-'A' में विघटन दर मिट्टी-'B' की अपेक्षा धीमी है।
options.B: मिट्टी-'A' में विघटन दर मिट्टी- B' की अपेक्षा तीव्र है।
options.C: दोनों में विघटन की दर एकसमान है।
options.D: नमूने A तथा B में कोई विघटन नहीं हुआ ।

options_english.A: Soil A has a slower rate of decomposition than Soil B.
options_english.B: Soil A has a faster rate of decomposition than Soil B.
options_english.C: Both have the same rate of decomposition.
options_english.D: No decomposition occurs in A and B.

questions.solution: The rate of decomposition is heavily influenced by the chemical composition of detritus. Decomposition is slower if the detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker if detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars. Soil Sample A has high lignin (40%) and chitin (45%) content and low nitrogen (5%) and sugar (10%). Soil Sample B has low lignin (5%) and chitin (15%) but high nitrogen (45%) and sugar (35%). Therefore, Soil A will have a slower rate of decomposition compared to Soil B.
questions.solution_hindi: विघटन की दर अपरद की रासायनिक संरचना से बहुत प्रभावित होती है। यदि अपरद लिग्निन और काइटिन से भरपूर है तो विघटन धीमा होता है, और यदि अपरद नाइट्रोजन और पानी में घुलनशील पदार्थों जैसे शर्करा से भरपूर है तो यह तेज होता है। मृदा नमूना A में उच्च लिग्निन (40%) और काइटिन (45%) सामग्री है और कम नाइट्रोजन (5%) और शर्करा (10%) है। मृदा नमूने B में लिग्निन (5%) और काइटिन (15%) कम है, लेकिन नाइट्रोजन (45%) और शर्करा (35%) अधिक है। इसलिए, मिट्टी B की तुलना में मिट्टी A के विघटन की दर धीमी होगी।

questions.text: मानव मादा में आर्तव चक्र में विभिन्न घटनाएँ होती हैं। उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसमें आर्तव चक्र की इन घटनाओं को सही अनुक्रम में दर्शाया गया है।
questions.text_english: Menstrual cycle in human females consists of various events. Select the option that indicates the correct sequence of these events of menstrual cycle.

options.A: ऋतुस्राव (रजोधर्म) प्रावस्था, पुटकीय प्रावस्था, स्रावी प्रावस्था, अंडोत्सर्ग प्रावस्था
options.B: स्रावी प्रावस्था, पुटकीय प्रावस्था, अंडोत्सर्ग प्रावस्था, ऋतुस्राव (रजोधर्म) प्रावस्था
options.C: ऋतुस्राव (रजोधर्म) प्रावस्था, पुटकीय प्रावस्था, अंडोत्सर्ग प्रावस्था, स्रावी प्रावस्था
options.D: पुटकीय प्रावस्था, स्रावी प्रावस्था, ऋतुस्राव (रजोधर्म) प्रावस्था, अंडोत्सर्ग प्रावस्था

options_english.B: Luteal phase, Follicular phase, Ovulatory phase, Menstrual phase
options_english.C: Menstrual phase, Follicular phase, Ovulatory phase, Luteal phase
options_english.D: Follicular phase, Luteal phase, Menstrual phase, Ovulatory phase

questions.solution: The correct sequence of events in the human female menstrual cycle starts with the Menstrual phase (days 1-5), followed by the Follicular (proliferative) phase (days 6-13), then the Ovulatory phase (day 14), and finally the Luteal (secretory) phase (days 15-28).

questions.text: शुद्ध वंशक्रम वाले मटर के दो जनक पौधों के बीच द्विसंकर क्रॉस कराया जाता है, जो विपर्यासी विशेषक के बीज रंग और बीज आकार दो युग्मों में एक दूसरे से भिन्न हैं। $F_{2}$ पीढ़ी में फीनोटाइप तथा जीनोटाइप की संख्या होगी -
questions.text_english: A Dihybrid cross is done between two parent pea plants (pure line) who differ in two pairs of contrasting traits: Seed colour and seed shape. In the $F_{2}$ generation the number of phenotypes and genotypes will be :
questions.solution: In a standard Mendelian dihybrid cross involving two pairs of contrasting traits, the F2 generation yields a phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1, which means there are 4 distinct phenotypes. The genotypic ratio is 1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1, which means there are 9 distinct genotypes. Hence, the number of phenotypes is 4 and genotypes is 9.
questions.solution_hindi: विपर्यासी विशेषकों के दो जोड़े से जुड़े एक मानक मेंडेलियन डायहाइब्रिड क्रॉस में, F2 पीढ़ी 9:3:3:1 का फीनोटाइपिक अनुपात उत्पन्न करती है, जिसका अर्थ है कि 4 अलग-अलग फीनोटाइप हैं। जीनोटाइपिक अनुपात 1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1 है, जिसका अर्थ है कि 9 अलग-अलग जीनोटाइप हैं। इसलिए, फीनोटाइप की संख्या 4 है और जीनोटाइप 9 है।

questions.text: आरएनए अंतरक्षेप (RNAi) तंबाकू के पौधे को सूत्रकृमि (मेलॉइडोजिन इनकोगनीशिया) के प्रति प्रतिरोधी बनाने में सहायक है। उचित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसके द्वारा ज्ञात हो सके कि आरएनए अंतक्षेपी किस प्रकार प्राप्त किया जाता है :
questions.text_english: RNA interference (RNAi) helps in making tobacco-plant resistant to a nematode (Meloidegyne incognita). Choose the correct option that shows how RNAi is achieved:

options.A: सूत्रकृमि के एमआरएनए के रूपांतरण प्रक्रम का अवरोधन ।
options.B: सूत्रकृमि के डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन को अवरोधित करना ।
options.C: पौधे के डीएनए के अनुलेखन को अवरोधित करना ।
options.D: पौधे के डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन को अवरोधित करना ।

options_english.A: Preventing the process of translation of mRNA of the nematode.
options_english.B: Preventing the process of replication of DNA of the nematode.
options_english.C: Preventing the process of transcription of DNA of the plant.
options_english.D: Preventing the process of replication of DNA of the plant.

questions.solution: RNA interference (RNAi) is a method of cellular defense which involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA (silencing). In the case of nematode-resistant tobacco plants, the introduction of nematode-specific genes leads to the formation of both sense and antisense RNA, which form dsRNA that initiates RNAi, ultimately silencing the specific mRNA of the nematode, preventing its translation into proteins.
questions.solution_hindi: आरएनए अंतरक्षेप (RNAi) कोशिकीय रक्षा की एक विधि है जिसमें एक पूरक dsRNA अणु के कारण एक विशिष्ट mRNA का शमन होता है जो mRNA को बांधता है और उसके अनुवाद को रोकता है। सूत्रकृमि-प्रतिरोधी तंबाकू पौधों के मामले में, सूत्रकृमि-विशिष्ट जीनों की शुरूआत से सेंस और एंटीसेंस आरएनए दोनों का निर्माण होता है, जो dsRNA बनाते हैं और RNAi शुरू करते हैं, अंततः सूत्रकृमि के विशिष्ट mRNA को शांत करते हैं, और प्रोटीन में इसके रूपांतरण (अनुवादन) को रोकते हैं।

questions.text: एक डीएनए खंड की कोडिंग रज्जु में नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों का अनुक्रम 5' -AATGCTAGGCAC - 3' है। इस डीएनए द्वारा अनुलेखित 'm-आरएनए' में नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों का सही अनुक्रम दर्शाने वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: The sequence of nitrogenous bases in a segment of a coding strand of DNA is $5^{\prime}$-AATGCTAGGCAC 3'. Choose the option that shows the correct sequence of nitrogenous bases in the mRNA transcribed by the DNA.
questions.solution: During transcription, the mRNA sequence is complementary to the template strand and identical to the coding strand, with the only difference being that Thymine (T) is replaced by Uracil (U) in RNA. Given the coding strand sequence 5'-AATGCTAGGCAC-3', the mRNA sequence will be exactly the same, but with 'U' instead of 'T': 5'-AAUGCUAGGCAC-3'.
questions.solution_hindi: अनुलेखन के दौरान, mRNA अनुक्रम टेम्प्लेट रज्जु के पूरक और कोडिंग रज्जु के समान होता है, एकमात्र अंतर यह है कि RNA में थाइमिन (T) को यूरैसिल (U) द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किया जाता है। दिए गए कोडिंग रज्जु अनुक्रम 5'-AATGCTAGGCAC-3' को देखते हुए, mRNA अनुक्रम बिल्कुल समान होगा, लेकिन 'T' के बजाय 'U' के साथ: 5'-AAUGCUAGGCAC-3'।

questions.text: एक व्यक्ति जिसके पिता वर्णांध थे, एक ऐसी स्त्री के साथ विवाह करता है जिसकी माता वर्णांध तथा पिता सामान्य दृष्टि वाले थे । इस युगल के कितने प्रतिशत पुत्र वर्णांध होंगे ?
questions.text_english: A man whose father was colour-blind marries a woman who had a colour-blind mother and normal father. What percentage of male children of this couple will be colour-blind?
questions.solution: Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait. The man receives his X chromosome from his mother and his Y chromosome from his colour-blind father. Since the man is not stated to be colour-blind, his genotype is XY (he does not inherit his father's defective X). The woman has a colour-blind mother ($X^cX^c$) and a normal father (XY), so she must receive the defective $X^c$ allele from her mother and a normal X allele from her father, making her a carrier ($XX^c$). When this man (XY) and woman ($XX^c$) have children, the male children receive their Y chromosome from the father and their X chromosome from the mother. They have a 50% chance of receiving the normal X allele and a 50% chance of receiving the defective $X^c$ allele. Therefore, 50% of the male children will be colour-blind.
questions.solution_hindi: वर्णांधता एक X-सहलग्न अप्रभावी गुण है। व्यक्ति (पुरुष) अपना X गुणसूत्र अपनी माँ से और अपना Y गुणसूत्र अपने वर्णांध पिता से प्राप्त करता है। चूँकि व्यक्ति वर्णांध नहीं है, उसका जीनोटाइप XY है (उसे अपने पिता का दोषपूर्ण X नहीं मिलता है)। स्त्री की माता वर्णांध ($X^cX^c$) और पिता सामान्य (XY) थे, इसलिए उसे अपनी माँ से दोषपूर्ण $X^c$ एलील और अपने पिता से सामान्य X एलील प्राप्त होना चाहिए, जिससे वह संवाहक ($XX^c$) बन जाती है। जब इस पुरुष (XY) और महिला ($XX^c$) के बच्चे होते हैं, तो नर बच्चे अपना Y गुणसूत्र पिता से और अपना X गुणसूत्र माता से प्राप्त करते हैं। उनके पास सामान्य X एलील प्राप्त करने की 50% संभावना है और दोषपूर्ण $X^c$ एलील प्राप्त करने की 50% संभावना है। इसलिए, 50% नर बच्चे वर्णांध होंगे।

questions.text: आधुनिक मानव के विकास में निम्नलिखित मानव सदृश्य नर वानर गण (प्राइमेट्स) सम्मिलित हैं। मानव विकास के सही अनुक्रम वाले विकल्प को चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Evolution of modern man involves the following man-like primates. Choose the correct series of human evolution.

options.A: ड्रायोपिथेकस → होमो इरेक्टस → ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो सैपियंस
options.B: ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो इरैक्टस → नियंडरथल → होमो सैपियंस
options.D: होमो इरैक्टस → ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो सैपियंस → नियंडरथल

options_english.A: Dryopithecus → Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens
options_english.B: Australopithecines → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
options_english.D: Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens → Neanderthal

questions.solution: The universally accepted correct evolutionary sequence of human ancestors is: Dryopithecus → Ramapithecus → Australopithecines → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal man → Homo sapiens. Option B is the only one that correctly follows this established chronological order.
questions.solution_hindi: मानव पूर्वजों का सार्वभौमिक रूप से स्वीकृत सही विकासवादी क्रम है: ड्रायोपिथेकस → रामापिथेकस → ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो हैबिलिस → होमो इरैक्टस → नियंडरथल मानव → होमो सैपियंस। विकल्प B एकमात्र ऐसा है जो इस स्थापित कालानुक्रमिक क्रम का सही ढंग से पालन करता है।

questions.text: 'जी ई एसी' का पूरा नाम है :
questions.text_english: GEAC stands for
questions.solution: The Indian Government has set up an organization called GEAC, which stands for Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (now technically called Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee, but Approval is standard in textbooks). It makes decisions regarding the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM-organisms for public services.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत सरकार ने GEAC नामक एक संगठन की स्थापना की है, जिसका अर्थ है जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग एप्रूवल कमेटी (Genetic Engineering Approval Committee)। यह जीएम अनुसंधान की वैधता और सार्वजनिक सेवाओं के लिए जीएम-जीवों को पेश करने की सुरक्षा के संबंध में निर्णय लेता है।

questions.text: कुछ रोगियों में ऊतक /अंग प्रत्यारोपण अकसर रोगी के ऊतकों/अंगों द्वारा अस्वीकृत किए जाने के कारण असफल हो जाता है। इस प्रकार की अस्वीकृति के लिए उत्तरदायी प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया का प्रकार है :
questions.text_english: Transplantation of tissues/organs to some patients often fails due to rejection of such tissues/organs by the body of the patient. Which type of immune response is responsible for such rejections?
questions.solution: The rejection of transplanted organs or tissues by the patient's body is primarily mediated by the cell-mediated immune response. T-lymphocytes (specifically cytotoxic T cells) recognize the grafted tissue as "non-self" and mount an immune attack against it, leading to graft rejection.
questions.solution_hindi: रोगी के शरीर द्वारा प्रत्यारोपित अंगों या ऊतकों की अस्वीकृति मुख्य रूप से कोशिका माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया (cell-mediated immune response) द्वारा होती है। T-लिम्फोसाइट्स (विशेष रूप से साइटोटॉक्सिक T कोशिकाएं) प्रत्यारोपित ऊतक को "बाहरी" (non-self) के रूप में पहचानते हैं और इसके खिलाफ प्रतिरक्षा हमला करते हैं, जिससे ग्राफ्ट की अस्वीकृति होती है।

questions.text: डी एन ए पॉलीमरेज का उपयोग करते हुए लाभकारी जीन को लगभग ________ गुना तक प्रवर्धित किया जा सकता है।

questions.text_english:
Study the two different crosses given below:
Cross I
Parents: 44 + XX  X  44 + XY
Gametes: 23 + X, 21 + X, 22 + X, 22 + Y
Offspring: 1
Cross II
Parents: 44 + XX  X  44 + XY
Gametes: 22 + XX, 22 + O, 22 + X, 22 + Y
Offspring: 2
Identify the abnormalities 1 and 2 in the offsprings of given crosses and distinguish between them.

key_points: Identify abnormality 1 as Down's Syndrome.
Identify abnormality 2 as Klinefelter's Syndrome.

Distinguish: Down's Syndrome is an autosomal disorder caused by trisomy of chromosome 21 (45+XX or 45+XY). Klinefelter's Syndrome is a sex-chromosomal disorder caused by the presence of an additional X chromosome in males (44+XXY).

questions.solution: In Cross I, the abnormal gamete '23 + X' indicates an extra autosome due to non-disjunction. When this fuses with a normal '22 + X' or '22 + Y' sperm, the offspring '1' will have 45 autosomes, resulting in Trisomy 21 or Down's syndrome. In Cross II, the abnormal gamete '22 + XX' indicates non-disjunction of sex chromosomes. When this fuses with a normal '22 + Y' sperm, the offspring '2' will have the genotype 44 + XXY, which is Klinefelter's syndrome. The primary distinction is that Down's syndrome is an autosomal aneuploidy (affecting chromosome 21), whereas Klinefelter's syndrome is a sex chromosome aneuploidy.

(A) एडीए विकार से पीड़ित एक रोगी को आवधिक अंतराल पर आनुवंशिकतः निर्मित लसीकाणुओं को प्रतिस्थापित कराना पड़ता है। इस प्रकार के आवधिक उपचार की आवश्यकता क्यों पड़ती है ? व्याख्या कीजिए।

sub_questions.text_english: (A) A patient with ADA deficiency requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes. Explain why such periodic infusion is required and also suggest a permanent cure for such ADA deficiency.

key_points: Explain periodic infusion requirement: The genetically engineered lymphocytes infused into the patient are not immortal; they have a definite lifespan and eventually die.
Suggest permanent cure: Introducing the gene isolate from marrow cells producing ADA into the cells of the patient at early embryonic stages.

sub_questions.solution: In gene therapy for ADA deficiency, lymphocytes from the patient's blood are grown in culture, and a functional ADA cDNA is introduced into them. These engineered cells are then returned to the patient. However, because these lymphocytes are somatic cells and not immortal, they eventually die off. Therefore, the patient requires periodic infusions of these genetically engineered lymphocytes to maintain adequate ADA levels. A permanent cure can be achieved if the functional gene isolated from bone marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into the cells of the patient during early embryonic stages, allowing all subsequent cells in the body to carry the correct gene.

sub_questions.text: (B) ऐसी किन्हीं दो तकनीकों का संक्षिप्त वर्णन कीजिए जिनका उपयोग किसी भी संवाहक जीव के बिना ही पुनर्योगज डीएनए को परपोषी कोशिका में सीधे ही प्रविष्ट कराने में किया जा सकता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) Describe in brief any two techniques that can be utilised to transfer recombinant DNA into the host cell directly without using any vector.

key_points: Technique 1: Micro-injection. Here, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell using a micro-pipette.
Technique 2: Biolistics or gene gun method. Here, cells (usually plant cells) are bombarded with high velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with the DNA.

sub_questions.solution:
Two vector-less methods for introducing recombinant DNA into host cells are: 
1. Micro-injection: This technique is primarily used for animal cells. The recombinant DNA is physically injected directly into the nucleus of the host cell using extremely fine glass needles or micro-pipettes.
2. Biolistics (Gene Gun): This method is highly suitable for plant cells. Target cells are bombarded with high-velocity microscopic particles of gold or tungsten that have been coated with the desired recombinant DNA.

sub_questions.text_english:
(A) Analyse the following ecosystems and discuss, which will be more productive in terms of primary productivity :
A young forest, a natural old forest, a shallow polluted lake.

key_points: Identify the most productive ecosystem: A shallow polluted lake.

Discuss why: The pollution in the lake often includes high levels of agricultural run-off rich in nutrients (nitrates and phosphates). This causes extreme eutrophication, leading to an explosive growth of phytoplankton and algae, resulting in exceptionally high primary productivity compared to terrestrial forests.

sub_questions.solution: Among the given ecosystems, a shallow polluted lake will be the most productive in terms of primary productivity. This is because polluted lakes typically suffer from cultural eutrophication due to the heavy influx of nutrient-rich agricultural or industrial run-off (containing high nitrates and phosphates). This vast overabundance of nutrients fuels explosive, rapid growth of algae and phytoplankton, leading to massive primary productivity rates that significantly exceed the more stable, balanced productivity seen in both young and natural old forests.

sub_questions.text: (B) एक पारिस्थितिक तंत्र की नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता तथा सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता के बीच विभेद कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) Differentiate between Net primary productivity and Gross primary productivity in an ecosystem.

key_points: Define Gross Primary Productivity (GPP): It is the total rate of production of organic matter (biomass) during photosynthesis by producers in an ecosystem.

Define Net Primary Productivity (NPP): It is the remaining biomass available for consumption to heterotrophs after subtracting the energy lost through respiration (R) by the producers from the GPP. (NPP = GPP - R).

sub_questions.solution: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) of an ecosystem refers to the absolute total rate at which solar energy is captured and converted into organic matter (biomass) through photosynthesis by primary producers. However, producers utilize a significant portion of this gross energy for their own metabolic processes (respiration). Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is defined as the gross primary productivity minus these respiratory losses (R). Therefore, NPP represents the actual net amount of new biomass generated that is physically available for consumption by the next trophic level (herbivores and decomposers). Mathematically, NPP = GPP - R.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Explain the importance of 'ori' and 'rop' in the E. coli cloning vector shown in the above given diagram.

key_points: Importance of 'ori': It is the essential origin of replication sequence. Any piece of foreign DNA linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within the host cells. It also controls the copy number of the linked DNA.

sub_questions.solution: In the pBR322 cloning vector, 'ori' designates the Origin of Replication. This is a highly specific DNA sequence where replication physically initiates. Its primary importance is that any foreign alien DNA linked to this precise sequence will be autonomously replicated and multiplied within the host bacterium. Furthermore, the 'ori' sequence dictates the final copy number of the plasmid. The 'rop' region is equally important as it specifically codes for essential proteins that mediate and regulate the entire replication process of the plasmid.

sub_questions.text: (b) एक्सोन्यूक्लिएज तथा एंडोन्यूक्लिएज के बीच विभेद कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Differentiate between exonucleases and endonucleases.

key_points: Differentiate Exonucleases: These enzymes act by removing nucleotides strictly from the terminal ends (either 5' or 3') of a DNA molecule.
Differentiate Endonucleases: These enzymes make specific, precise internal cuts at specific positions directly within the sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA molecule, rather than at the ends.

sub_questions.solution: Nucleases are enzymes that cleave the phosphodiester bonds of nucleic acids, and they are broadly classified into two main types. Exonucleases function by progressively removing nucleotides one by one strictly from the free terminal ends (either the 5' or 3' end) of the linear DNA strand. In stark contrast, Endonucleases do not act on the ends; instead, they recognize specific sequences and make precise internal cuts directly within the continuous sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA molecule.

sub_questions.solution: A palindromic nucleotide sequence in DNA reads the same on the two strands when reading orientation is kept the same (e.g., 5' to 3'). Therefore, the complementary sequence to the provided 5'-GAATTC-3' strand must be written ensuring the correct antiparallel polarity, which is exactly 3'-CTTAAG-5'.

sub_questions.text_english: (c) How are sticky ends produced? Mention their role.

key_points: Production: They are produced when restriction endonucleases make staggered cuts in the two strands of DNA, slightly away from the exact center of the palindromic recognition site, leaving overhanging single-stranded stretches.

Role: They facilitate the formation of recombinant DNA. Because they are complementary, they form weak hydrogen bonds with corresponding sticky ends created on the vector DNA, greatly facilitating the final action of the enzyme DNA ligase to join them permanently.

sub_questions.solution: Sticky ends are specialized single-stranded overhanging stretches of DNA. They are produced when certain restriction endonucleases (like EcoR I) deliberately do not cut the DNA straight across. Instead, they make staggered, off-center cuts in the two strands within the palindromic recognition site. The critical biological role of these sticky ends is to heavily facilitate the construction of recombinant DNA. Because they possess exposed complementary bases, they eagerly form weak, temporary hydrogen bonds with corresponding sticky ends on foreign DNA cut by the exact same enzyme. This initial stickiness holds the two pieces together, allowing the enzyme DNA ligase to efficiently follow up and permanently seal the sugar-phosphate backbones, creating stable recombinant DNA.

questions.text_english: Compare and contrast convergent and divergent evolution.

key_points: Explain Divergent Evolution: It is the evolutionary process where organisms descending from a single, common ancestor gradually diverge and develop different functional structures to adapt to completely different habitats or needs. It results in Homologous organs.
Provide Example of Divergent: Forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs, and humans (same basic skeletal structure but radically different functions like swimming, flying, running, grasping).

Explain Convergent Evolution: It is the evolutionary process where entirely unrelated groups of organisms, facing identical environmental pressures, independently evolve strikingly similar functional structures. It results in Analogous organs.
Provide Example of Convergent: The wings of butterflies and the wings of birds (structurally and anatomically completely different origins, but both evolved for the exact same function: flying).

questions.solution:
Divergent and convergent evolution represent two fundamentally opposing pathways in evolutionary biology. 
1. Origin and Direction: Divergent evolution occurs when a single ancestral species slowly splits and radiates into multiple new species adapting to diverse environmental niches; it moves from a common point outwards. Conversely, convergent evolution occurs when completely distinct and unrelated ancestral lineages are subjected to similar severe environmental pressures and independently evolve remarkably similar physical adaptations; it moves from different points towards a common functional design.
2. Organ Type: Because divergent evolution starts from a shared blueprint, it leads to the formation of Homologous organs—structures that share a deep anatomical and developmental similarity but perform vastly different functions. Convergent evolution, however, results in Analogous organs—structures that have completely different anatomical origins and underlying blueprints but perform the exact same superficial function.
3. Examples: A classic example of divergent evolution is the forelimbs of mammals. The flipper of a whale, the wing of a bat, and the arm of a human all share the same basic humerus-radius-ulna bone structure inherited from a common ancestor, but they are adapted for swimming, flying, and grasping, respectively. A prime example of convergent evolution is the wing of an insect (made of chitinous membrane) and the wing of a bird (made of feathers and bone); they share no common anatomical origin but both independently evolved the ability to fly to survive in an aerial environment.

अपसारी (Divergent) और अभिसारी (Convergent) विकास विकासवादी जीव विज्ञान में दो मौलिक रूप से विपरीत मार्ग हैं।
1. उत्पत्ति: अपसारी विकास तब होता है जब एक ही पूर्वज प्रजाति धीरे-धीरे विभिन्न पर्यावरणीय आवासों के अनुकूल होने के लिए कई नई प्रजातियों में विभाजित हो जाती है। इसके विपरीत, अभिसारी विकास तब होता है जब पूरी तरह से अलग और असंबंधित प्रजातियां समान पर्यावरणीय दबावों के कारण स्वतंत्र रूप से बहुत समान शारीरिक अनुकूलन विकसित करती हैं।
2. अंग का प्रकार: अपसारी विकास समजात अंगों (Homologous organs) के निर्माण की ओर जाता है - ऐसी संरचनाएं जो शारीरिक रूप से समान होती हैं लेकिन बहुत अलग कार्य करती हैं। अभिसारी विकास समवृत्ति अंगों (Analogous organs) में परिणत होता है - ऐसी संरचनाएं जिनकी उत्पत्ति बिल्कुल अलग होती है लेकिन वे एक ही कार्य करती हैं।

sub_questions.text: (a) उपरोक्त चित्र में दर्शाई गई संरचना को पहचानिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Identify the structure shown in the above figure.

sub_questions.solution: The provided diagram illustrates the fundamental, repeating structural unit of chromatin within a eukaryotic cell nucleus, which is scientifically identified as a Nucleosome.

sub_questions.text: (b) नामांकन 'P' तथा 'Q' को पहचानिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Identify the labels P and Q.

key_points: Identify P: Negatively charged DNA double helix wrapped around the core.
Identify Q: Histone octamer (the central protein core composed of 8 histone molecules).

sub_questions.solution: In the nucleosome structure, label 'P' clearly points to the long, thread-like structure winding around the central core, which represents the negatively charged DNA double helix. Label 'Q' indicates the solid central core structure itself, which is definitively the Histone octamer, a complex of eight specific histone proteins.

sub_questions.text: (c) हिस्टोन प्रोटीनों की प्रकृति लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Write the nature of histone proteins.

key_points: Explain nature: Histones are small, highly basic proteins.

Explain why: They carry a strong positive charge because their amino acid sequences are exceptionally rich in the basic amino acid residues lysines and arginines. This positive charge crucially allows them to tightly bind the negatively charged DNA.

sub_questions.solution: Histone proteins possess a very distinct biochemical nature: they are highly basic proteins carrying a strong overall positive charge. This characteristic basic nature arises because they are exceptionally rich in specific basic amino acid residues, primarily lysines and arginines. This strong positive charge is absolutely crucial, as it allows the histones to tightly attract and bind the highly negatively charged DNA molecules to form stable nucleosomes.

sub_questions.text: (d) यूक्रोमेटिन तथा हेटेरोक्रोमेटीन के बीच विभेद कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (d) Distinguish between Euchromatin and Heterochromatin.

key_points: Difference 1 (Packaging): Euchromatin is loosely packed and structurally less dense. Heterochromatin is very tightly packed and structurally highly dense.
Difference 2 (Staining): Due to loose packing, Euchromatin stains relatively light when treated with nuclear dyes. Conversely, tightly packed Heterochromatin stains very dark.
Difference 3 (Activity): Euchromatin is genetically active and transcriptionally active, allowing RNA polymerase access. Heterochromatin is genetically silenced and transcriptionally inactive.

sub_questions.solution:
Within a typical eukaryotic nucleus, chromatin exists in two distinct, functionally different forms based on its level of compaction. 
1. Euchromatin refers to regions where the chromatin fibers are relatively loosely packed. Because it is loosely assembled, it stains lightly when exposed to basic dyes. Crucially, this loose structure allows enzymes like RNA polymerase to easily access the DNA, making euchromatin highly transcriptionally active (genetically active).
2. Heterochromatin refers to regions where the chromatin is exceptionally densely and tightly packed. As a result of this extreme compaction, it stains very dark. The tight packing physically blocks access to the DNA, rendering heterochromatin transcriptionally inactive (genetically silenced).

questions.solution: The question demands identification of the nucleosome complex from the diagram, understanding the specific biochemical properties of its protein components, and differentiating between the two primary higher-order states of chromatin packaging in a cell nucleus.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
In nature, we rarely find isolated, single individuals of any species; majority of them live in groups in a well-defined geographical area, share or compete for similar resources, potentially interbreed and thus constitute a population. The population has certain attributes whereas, an individual organism does not. A population at a given time is composed of individuals of different ages. The size of the population tells us a lot about its status in the habitat. Whatever ecological processes we wish to investigate in a population, be it the outcome of competition with another species, the impact of the predator or the effect of pesticide application, we always evaluate in terms of any change in the population size. The size, in nature, could be low or go into millions. Population size, technically called population density (N) need not necessarily be measured in numbers only. The size of a population for any species is not a static parameter. It keeps on changing with time depending on various factors including food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather.
(a) The Monarch butterfly is highly distasteful to its predator because of a special chemical present in its body. How does the butterfly acquire this chemical?
(b) If population density at a timet $t+1$ is 800, Emigration $=100$, Immigration $=200$, Natality $=200$ and Mortality $=150$, calculate the population density at time t and comment upon the type of age pyramid that will be formed in this case.
Student to attempt either sub-part (c) or (d):
(c) What is the difference in a method of measuring population density in an area if there are 200 carrot grass plants to only single huge banyan tree?
OR
(d) Name two methods to measure the population density of tigers.

sub_questions.text: (a) मोनार्क तितली के शरीर में पाए जाने वाले विशेष रसायन के कारण यह अपने परभक्षी के लिए बहुत ही अरुचिकर है। तितली यह रसायन किस प्रकार प्राप्त करती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) The Monarch butterfly is highly distasteful to its predator because of a special chemical present in its body. How does the butterfly acquire this chemical?

key_points: Identify acquisition method: It aggressively acquires this highly toxic, distasteful chemical explicitly during its developmental caterpillar stage.
Identify source: The caterpillar achieves this by deliberately feeding on a highly poisonous weed (milkweed).

sub_questions.solution: The Monarch butterfly successfully defends itself against avian predators by harboring a highly potent, distasteful chemical compound within its body. It does not synthesize this chemical itself; rather, it ingeniously acquires it during its early developmental caterpillar stage. It does this by deliberately seeking out and voraciously feeding upon a specific poisonous weed, commonly milkweed, safely sequestering the plant's natural toxins into its own tissues.

sub_questions.text: (b) यदि किसी जाति का समष्टि घनत्व एक समय $t+1=800,$ उत्प्रवासन $=100$, आप्रवासन $=200$ जन्मदर $=200$ तथा मृत्युदर $=150$ है, तो उस समय 't' पर समष्टि दर का परिकलन कीजिए तथा इस केस में बनने वाले आयु पिरैमिड के प्रकार पर समीक्षा (टिप्पणी) कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) If population density at a timet $t+1$ is 800, Emigration $=100$, Immigration $=200$, Natality $=200$ and Mortality $=150$, calculate the population density at time t and comment upon the type of age pyramid that will be formed in this case.

key_points: State population equation: N(t+1) = Nt + [(B + I) - (D + E)]
Substitute given values: 800 = Nt + [(200 + 200) - (150 + 100)]

Comment on pyramid: Since N(t+1) (800) is significantly greater than Nt (650), the population is clearly expanding. Therefore, an upright, triangular, or expanding age pyramid will be formed, characterizing a growing population with a broad base of pre-reproductive individuals.

sub_questions.solution: To calculate the initial population density at time t (Nt), we utilize the fundamental ecological equation governing population growth: N(t+1) = Nt + [(B + I) - (D + E)], where B is Natality, I is Immigration, D is Mortality, and E is Emigration. Substituting the provided data: 800 = Nt + [(200 + 200) - (150 + 100)]. This simplifies to 800 = Nt + [400 - 250], and further to 800 = Nt + 150. Solving for Nt, we find the initial population density Nt = 800 - 150 = 650 individuals. Regarding the age pyramid, since the population has grown substantially from 650 to 800, it indicates an actively expanding population. In such populations, the number of young (pre-reproductive) individuals far exceeds older ones. Graphically, this invariably results in a classic expanding, upright, or triangular-shaped age pyramid with a very broad base.

sub_questions.text: (c) किसी क्षेत्र में 200 गाजर घास वाले पौधों तथा केवल एक विशालकाय बरगद के वृक्ष के समष्टि घनत्व को मापने की विधि में क्या अंतर है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (c) What is the difference in a method of measuring population density in an area if there are 200 carrot grass plants to only single huge banyan tree?

key_points: Explain measurement for carrot grass: Because there are many small individual plants, measuring by simple total number (counting individuals) is the most appropriate and accurate method.

Explain measurement for banyan tree: Counting just 'one' tree completely misrepresents its massive ecological dominance. Therefore, measuring total biomass or percent cover (canopy area) is the biologically meaningful measure of its population density.

sub_questions.solution: Population density is typically measured by simply counting the total number of individuals, which works perfectly for the 200 small carrot grass (Parthenium) plants, establishing their numerical dominance. However, applying this same total number method to the banyan tree is severely misleading. Stating there is only "one" banyan tree completely fails to account for its massive size and profound ecological footprint. Therefore, for a single, gigantic organism like a banyan tree, the appropriate method for measuring population density is to calculate its total biomass or assess its extensive percent cover (the vast area shadowed by its canopy), which truly reflects its significant ecological role in that specific habitat.

sub_questions.text: (d) बाघ की समष्टि घनत्व के मापन की दो विधियों (तरीकों) के नाम लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (d) Name two methods to measure the population density of tigers.

key_points: Method 1: Pug marks (analyzing the unique footprints left by individual tigers).
Method 2: Fecal pellets (analyzing scats for DNA identification) or utilizing motion-activated camera traps for photographic identification based on unique stripe patterns.

sub_questions.solution: Given the incredibly elusive and dangerous nature of wild tigers, ecologists cannot reliably count them directly. Instead, they rely on highly effective indirect methods to estimate their population density. Two primary methods utilized in national parks and reserves involve meticulously tracking and analyzing their unique pug marks (footprints), which act like individual fingerprints. Secondly, researchers heavily rely on advanced analysis of fecal pellets (scats) for DNA profiling, or increasingly, they deploy networks of hidden, motion-activated camera traps to photographically identify individual tigers based entirely on their distinctly unique stripe patterns.

sub_questions.text: (a) 'केस-1' तथा 'केस-2' में किस हॉर्मोन का स्तर शीर्षस्थ है ? इस हॉर्मोन का एक प्रकार्य लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Which hormone is responsible for the peak observed in Case 1 and Case 2? Write one function of that hormone.

key_points: Identify hormone: Luteinizing Hormone (LH) is fundamentally responsible for the massive, sharp mid-cycle peak (LH surge) clearly seen directly preceding ovulation in both graphs.
State function: This intense, sudden surge in LH decisively induces the physical rupture of the fully mature Graafian follicle, thereby causing ovulation (release of the ovum).

sub_questions.solution: In both graphical representations of the female reproductive cycle, the prominent, sharp peak labeled 'P' occurring precisely before ovulation strictly represents the Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge. This massive, sudden increase in LH concentration serves a critical biological function: it directly stimulates and induces the rapid physical rupture of the fully mature Graafian follicle, compelling it to release its secondary oocyte in the pivotal event universally known as ovulation.

sub_questions.text: (b) पुटकीय (प्रचुरोद्भवन) प्रावस्था की अवधि में अंडाशय तथा गर्भाशय में होने वाले परिवर्तनों को लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Write changes that take place in the ovary and uterus during follicular phase.

key_points: Ovarian changes: Primary follicles grow, develop, and eventually mature into a single, fully developed Graafian follicle.

Uterine changes: The severely sloughed off endometrium lining of the uterus actively regenerates and thickens rapidly through massive cellular proliferation, heavily driven by increasing estrogen levels.

sub_questions.solution: During the highly active follicular phase of the menstrual cycle, significant parallel changes occur in two organs. In the ovary, stimulated by FSH, several primary follicles begin to grow, but usually, only one successfully matures completely into a large, fluid-filled Graafian follicle. Simultaneously, in the uterus, the inner glandular lining known as the endometrium, which was previously shed during menstruation, begins to actively regenerate. It rapidly thickens and heavily re-vascularizes through intense cellular proliferation, a repair process strictly driven by the rising levels of estrogens secreted by the developing ovarian follicles.

sub_questions.text: (c) केस-2 के हॉर्मोन-Q का नाम लिखिए तथा इसका एक प्रकार्य भी लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Name the hormone Q of Case 2. Write one function of hormone Q.

key_points: Identify Hormone Q: Progesterone. (In Case 2, it continuously rises instead of dropping, indicating pregnancy).

State function: Its primary function is to heavily maintain and actively support the thickened uterine endometrium, creating an ideal environment absolutely essential for embryo implantation and the continuous maintenance of the pregnancy.

sub_questions.solution: In Case 2, the graph illustrates that fertilization and successful implantation have clearly occurred, evidenced by the presence of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (HCG). Consequently, hormone 'Q', which steadily continues to rise and remain extraordinarily high during the luteal phase instead of declining, is identified as Progesterone. The paramount physiological function of massive progesterone secretion is to actively sustain and heavily maintain the thick, vascularized endometrial lining of the uterus. This maintenance is absolutely vital; without it, the lining would slough off, terminating the pregnancy. It provides the essential, secure environment necessary for continued embryonic development.

sub_questions.text: (d) 'केस-2' में अण्डाशय की कौन सी संरचना क्रियाशील रह जाएगी ? यह कैसे बनती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (d) Which structure in the ovary will remain functional in Case 2? How is it formed?

key_points: Identify structure: The Corpus Luteum will remain highly functional and active.

Explain formation: It is biologically formed from the remaining cellular parts of the ruptured Graafian follicle immediately following ovulation, undergoing structural transformation under the heavy influence of LH.

sub_questions.solution: In Case 2, which clearly depicts a state of pregnancy characterized by the presence of HCG preventing luteal regression, the crucial ovarian structure that will persist and remain highly functional is the Corpus Luteum. Following the dramatic event of ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle does not simply disappear. In a mature angiosperm pollen grain (male gametophyte), the internal space is partitioned into two unequal cells. The massive Vegetative cell acts as a vital reservoir, possessing abundant food reserves and a large, irregularly shaped nucleus; its primary destiny is to guide the formation of the pollen tube. The diminutive Generative cell is distinctly spindle-shaped with a dense nucleus and physically floats suspended within the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell; its crucial destiny is to undergo mitotic division to yield two functional male gametes for double fertilization. 
Looking at the diagram of pollination vectors: 
Arrow '1' depicts pollen moving from the anther to the stigma of the very same flower, which is technically defined as Autogamy. 
Arrow '2' depicts pollen traversing from one flower to the stigma of a completely different flower that resides on the exact same plant, which is technically defined as Geitonogamy. 
Arrow '3' depicts pollen traveling from one flower to the stigma of a flower situated on a totally separate plant, which is technically defined as Xenogamy (true cross-pollination). 
Regarding specific aquatic plant pollination: The Water lily, although firmly rooted underwater, pushes its vibrant flowers above the water surface; consequently, it cannot use water for pollination and instead relies heavily on flying insects or wind. Conversely, Vallisneria utilizes true hydrophily; its female flowers reach the water surface while male flowers detach and float freely, relying entirely on gentle water currents to physically bring them together. 
The immense biological advantage of Xenogamy (method 3) is genetic recombination. Because it brings together pollen and eggs from genetically distinct plants, it introduces vital genetic variation into the offspring, ensuring enhanced evolutionary fitness and actively preventing the detrimental genetic decline known as inbreeding depression.

(ii) Role of Zona Pellucida: The moment the first sperm contacts it, the zona pellucida undergoes immediate, massive structural changes (hardening) that forcefully block the entry of any additional sperms, thus strictly preventing fatal polyspermy.

By carefully analyzing the provided diagram of fertilization, the distinct fates of the three sperms become clear. Sperm 'P' is the undisputed winner; it has aggressively battled through the corona radiata and zona pellucida and has made physical contact with the ovum's delicate plasma membrane. This contact ensures it will successfully inject its nucleus and fertilize the egg. Sperms 'Q' and 'R' are late arrivals. Sperm 'Q' has breached the corona radiata but is stopped cold by the zona pellucida, while Sperm 'R' remains entirely on the outside. Both Q and R will rapidly exhaust their energy reserves and die without contributing genetically. 
The crucial role of the thick Zona pellucida layer is purely protective. The exact millisecond Sperm 'P' makes contact, it induces profound, irreversible structural changes within the zona pellucida, essentially turning it into a concrete wall. This absolute hardening effectively blocks all other sperms from entering, ensuring that only one sperm fertilizes the egg, thereby strictly preventing the lethal condition of polyspermy. 
The entry of Sperm 'P' initiates a dramatic biological awakening within the dormant ovum. The secondary oocyte, which had been permanently stalled in metaphase of meiosis II, is suddenly triggered to resume and finally complete its meiotic division. This division is highly asymmetrical, resulting in the creation of a massive, nutrient-rich, functional haploid ovum (the ootid) and the extrusion of a tiny, non-functional second polar body. 
In the arduous journey to achieve fertilization, the structural components of the sperm are indispensable. The Acrosome, forming the cap of the sperm head, operates as a biological drill; it is heavily loaded with potent lytic enzymes (like hyaluronidase) that literally digest a physical tunnel through the tough protective layers of the ovum. Simultaneously, the Middle piece acts as the sperm's powerhouse. It is densely packed with tightly coiled mitochondria that furiously generate tremendous amounts of ATP. This energy is singularly dedicated to fueling the relentless, whip-like lashing of the sperm's tail, providing the intense motility required to physically swim through the female reproductive tract to reach the ovum.

(ii) Cytokine barriers are a component of innate immunity. Virus-infected cells secrete specialized protective proteins called interferons. These interferons powerfully act to protect adjacent, non-infected healthy cells from further viral infection.

sub_questions.solution:
MALT, which fully expands to Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue, constitutes a massive portion of the human immune system. It is strategically located as a protective barrier within the lining of all major exposed internal tracts, prominently including the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts, guarding against constant microbial entry. 
Cytokine barriers form a highly crucial, fast-acting component of our innate immune system. When host cells are tragically infected by a virus, they altruistically secrete specialized antiviral proteins known universally as interferons. These interferons rapidly travel to and coat adjacent healthy cells, preemptively protecting them from succumbing to further viral infection, thus breaking the chain of viral spread. 
The primary diagnostic test relied upon globally for confirming AIDS is ELISA, which stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. This sophisticated test operates entirely on the foundational immunological principle of highly specific antigen-antibody interactions, detecting the presence of HIV antigens or the body's specific antibodies against them. 
Within the human immune system, the Bone marrow and Thymus reign supreme as the two primary lymphoid organs. They achieve their vital roles through distinct functions. The Bone marrow is the ultimate biological factory; it is the site where all blood cells, including both B and T lymphocytes, are initially generated from stem cells. Furthermore, it serves as the exclusive environment for the complete maturation of B-lymphocytes. Conversely, the Thymus, a lobed organ near the heart, acts as an elite training academy. It provides the highly specialized micro-environment that is absolutely necessary for immature T-lymphocytes (which migrate from the marrow) to undergo rigorous differentiation and achieve full immunological maturation, becoming ready to combat diseases.

(A) (i) Haemophilia and red green colourblindness is usually observed in men. Why?
(ii) Perform a cross(es) where haemophilic daughter(s) and haemophilic son(s) are produced in same ratio.

key_points: (i) Explain occurrence in men: Both diseases are X-linked recessive genetic disorders. Males possess only a single X chromosome (XY). Therefore, inheriting just one single defective, mutated gene on their solitary X chromosome from their mother is absolutely sufficient to manifest the disease.
(ii) Perform cross: For equal ratios of affected sons and daughters, a Carrier Female ($X^hX$) must be mated with an Affected Haemophilic Male ($X^hY$).

(ii) Show the cross results: The resulting offspring genotypes are $X^hX^h$ (haemophilic daughter), $X^hX$ (carrier daughter), $X^hY$ (haemophilic son), and XY (normal son). This perfectly yields a 1:1 ratio of haemophilic daughters to haemophilic sons (25% of total offspring each).

sub_questions.solution:
Haemophilia and red-green colour blindness are classic examples of sex-linked recessive genetic disorders, specifically meaning the defective mutated genes are located exclusively on the X chromosome. These severe disorders are disproportionately observed in men rather than women due to fundamental chromosomal differences. Males possess a heterogametic sex chromosome constitution (XY), possessing only one single X chromosome. Consequently, if a male inherits just one single defective allele on his solitary X chromosome from his carrier mother, he completely lacks a corresponding normal dominant allele on the Y chromosome to mask it. Therefore, a single dose of the defective gene is absolutely sufficient to fully manifest the disease in men. Females, however, are homogametic (XX) and require two copies of the defective allele (one from each parent) to be affected, a statistical rarity.
To artificially produce a genetic scenario where haemophilic daughters and haemophilic sons are generated in the exact same 1:1 ratio, a very specific mating must occur. We must perform a genetic cross between a Carrier Female (who is phenotypically normal but carries the hidden defect, genotype $X^hX$) and an Affected Haemophilic Male (genotype $X^hY$). When we map this cross: the carrier mother produces two types of ova ($X^h$ and X), and the affected father produces two types of sperm ($X^h$ and Y). The possible fertilizations yield four distinct offspring genotypes: $X^hX^h$ (a haemophilic daughter), $X^hX$ (a normal carrier daughter), $X^hY$ (a haemophilic son), and XY (a completely normal son). Analysing these results clearly shows that 25% of the total offspring are haemophilic daughters and exactly 25% are haemophilic sons, flawlessly achieving the requested equal 1:1 ratio of affected male and female progeny.

key_points: (i) Bacteria location: Since bacteria lack a defined nucleus, both transcription and translation occur simultaneously within the common cytoplasm.

(i) Eukaryotes location: The two processes are strictly separated; Transcription occurs exclusively deep within the protected Nucleus, whereas Translation occurs externally out in the Cytoplasm (often on ribosomes attached to the rough ER).

(ii) Draw replication fork: A neat Y-shaped structure must be drawn. It must clearly label the two template strands with opposite polarities (3'->5' and 5'->3'). It must prominently show the 'continuous synthesis' forming the leading strand on the 3'->5' template, and the 'discontinuous synthesis' forming fragmented Okazaki fragments on the 5'->3' template.

(iii) Calculation: According strictly to Chargaff's rule in double-stranded DNA, the total number of Purines (Adenine + Guanine) always perfectly equals the total number of Pyrimidines (Thymine + Cytosine). Therefore, if a DNA segment contains a total of 1000 nucleotides, exactly half of them must invariably be pyrimidines. The number of pyrimidines is 500.

sub_questions.solution:
The fundamental locations of gene expression processes differ vastly between bacteria and eukaryotes. In primitive bacteria, which totally lack a nuclear membrane compartmentalizing their genetic material, both the transcription of DNA into mRNA and the subsequent translation of that mRNA into proteins occur simultaneously right within the fluid Cytoplasm. In stark contrast, highly evolved eukaryotes employ strict spatial separation. Transcription occurs exclusively within the protected confines of the Nucleus, and the fully processed mRNA must then be exported out to the Cytoplasm, where translation occurs on the ribosomes.
For the diagram of the DNA replication fork, a Y-shaped unzipped section of a DNA double helix should be clearly sketched. The critical feature to label is polarity: one exposed template strand must run 3' to 5', upon which the new DNA is synthesized smoothly as one long, continuous piece called the leading strand. The opposing template strand must run 5' to 3', upon which the new DNA is forced to be synthesized backwards in short, discontinuous, disjointed segments known famously as Okazaki fragments, collectively forming the lagging strand.
The mathematical calculation is elegantly simple and relies entirely on Erwin Chargaff's fundamental rules of base pairing for double-stranded DNA molecules. Chargaff dictates that Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T), and Guanine (G) always pairs with Cytosine (C). Because Purines (A and G) always pair strictly with Pyrimidines (T and C), the total combined number of purine bases in any double-stranded DNA molecule must always exactly equal the total combined number of pyrimidine bases. The provided detail about 240 Adenine nucleotides is deliberately extraneous information designed to confuse. If the entire DNA segment comprises exactly 1000 nucleotides in total, then mathematically, precisely half of those nucleotides must be purines and the other half must be pyrimidines. Therefore, without any complex calculation, the total number of pyrimidine bases in this specific segment is definitively 500.
